attacks.claim: Launch auto-download silently replaces the local slot when only the cloud copy is newer. This contradicts the 'nothing is overwritten without that choice' guarantee and the public 'saves stay where they are' copy.
attacks.evidence: 'On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older.' vs 'Nothing is overwritten without that choice.' and 'Your saves on this PC stay where they are.'

attacks.claim: 'Newer' is decided by wall-clock last-modified timestamps written by different PCs. Clock skew can make an older save look newer and be silently replaced.
attacks.evidence: 'downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older' / ABSENT: clock source, skew tolerance, or a revision/version counter

attacks.claim: 'Changed since last sync' is never defined. No base revision or last-synced state is recorded per slot, so the client cannot reliably distinguish 'both changed' from 'one changed'. The conflict prompt can be skipped or shown wrongly.
attacks.evidence: 'If both changed since last sync, the game asks' / ABSENT: how the last-synced state is recorded and compared

attacks.claim: The retention guarantee is false as written. Only 5 server versions and 3 local backups are kept, so older replaced versions are dropped on the next replacement. This conflicts with the agreed 'never lose a save' requirement.
attacks.evidence: 'Every replaced version is kept: the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally in saves/backup/'

attacks.claim: The client does not validate before uploading. A valid-but-bad local save (for example, after a bug) can be uploaded repeatedly, up to 60 times an hour, and push out all 5 good server versions.
attacks.evidence: 'the server never parses them' / '60 uploads per hour per player' / ABSENT: client-side validation before upload

attacks.claim: The 1.3 round trip is only tested for loading. Nothing shows that 1.3 preserves the new option keys and sidecar when it saves, or that a 1.4 re-upgrade after 1.3 play handles the stale baseline. Either case could drop modifiers or pull an older cloud copy over 1.3 progress.
attacks.evidence: QA row: 'Downgrade to 1.3 ... Loads, sidecar and modifier keys ignored' / ABSENT: return-to-1.4 test after 1.3 play

attacks.claim: The rollback path is only tested on a Steam beta branch. The Epic downgrade (29% of players) is not shown to work, and changing the default branch does not revert already-installed 1.4 clients.
attacks.evidence: '1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores' vs QA: 'Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch 1.3-legacy)' and 'the Epic dev sandbox'

attacks.claim: Server-side enforcement for EOS-restricted (under-13) accounts is not stated. The restriction is described only as UI behaviour, so a modified client or direct API call could create a link for a restricted account.
attacks.evidence: 'for them linking is not offered and the screen explains why.' / ABSENT: server rejection of link requests for EOS-restricted accounts

attacks.claim: Minor protection covers only Epic cabined accounts. Steam players and non-cabined Epic players, including EU age-of-consent cases, get no age gate or parental-consent path. It is also unclear whether a cabined account can enable Cross-Save and upload save and sync.meta data without linking.
attacks.evidence: 'Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered' / ABSENT: age gate or parental consent for Steam or non-cabined accounts; ABSENT: upload/sync test for cabined accounts

attacks.claim: The data inventory says no name data is stored, but the sync.meta sidecar includes a device name, which can contain a real name. The disclosure does not match what is stored.
attacks.evidence: 'No email, name, payment or friends data.' vs 'sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)'

attacks.claim: The beta and QA ran against the production backend, collecting real Steam and Epic IDs and links from Nov 18-30. The artifact does not show that a privacy notice covering that collection was live during the beta.
attacks.evidence: 'pointed at the production Cross-Save backend' and 'Nov 18-30: public opt-in beta' vs 'linked from the Cross-Save screen before linking' (no date)

attacks.claim: The deletion promise covers save copies but does not address the link record's retention, logs or telemetry that pair steam_id with epic_account_id, dashboard data, or whether deletion reaches backups and replicas.
attacks.evidence: 'removes the link and all server copies within 24 h' / ABSENT: retention for link table, logs, dashboards, backups and replicas

attacks.claim: Unlink-and-delete authorization is unspecified. If a single store session or token is enough, a stolen session could irreversibly delete a victim's server saves and their 5-version history.
attacks.evidence: 'Unlink and delete cloud saves' removes the link and all server copies within 24 h / ABSENT: re-authentication or dual-session requirement for unlink and delete

attacks.claim: The client uses slot and device-name values from sync.meta, which are server-stored and server-returned, to place backup files. No validation or path-safety rule is stated, so crafted values could steer local writes outside saves/.
attacks.evidence: 'sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)' and 'keeps the last 3 locally in saves/backup/' / ABSENT: sidecar field validation and slot-to-path mapping

attacks.claim: Multi-slot sync has no atomicity or partial-failure handling. A failure after some slot blobs or the sidecar are uploaded can leave the server with a blob and sidecar that disagree, and no reconciliation is described.
attacks.evidence: 'Sync uploads the existing save slots plus a small sync.meta sidecar' / ABSENT: transaction, ordering, or reconciliation

attacks.claim: The whole base goes live on one morning, and about 109k opt-in players can hit first-time sync at once. The only load test is 30k launches over 10 minutes, with no ramp, canary, or peak-to-average model.
attacks.evidence: 'Dec 2 10:00 PT: 1.4 to all players on both stores' / 'Load test: 30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min | p95 410 ms, 0 errors'

attacks.claim: Storage is not bounded globally, and the forecast does not follow from the caps. At 10 slots x 5 versions x 420 KB, one player holds about 21 MB, so 109k opted-in players reach about 2.3 TB, not the forecast 140 GB. Worst case per player is about 100 MB, and no global quota is stated.
attacks.evidence: '~420 KB per slot x up to 5 versions; forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month' / 'accepts max 2 MB per slot, 10 slots per player'

attacks.claim: The $600 hard stop is not shown to cap spend. Its mechanism and billing lag are unspecified, and it depends on the same project and server config it must stop. Clients retry on launch and every 10 min, so requests can continue after the stop, and the automated kill-switch flip has no failure path.
attacks.evidence: 'hard project budget stop at $600/month; at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically' / 'read on launch and every 10 min'

attacks.claim: The kill switch and the automatic budget-triggered flip, which are the primary rollback path, have no QA test. Their behaviour is asserted in prose only.
attacks.evidence: 'Kill switch cross_save_enabled=false' / 'at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically' vs QA summary with no kill-switch or re-enable row

attacks.claim: Beta results (0 lost saves, 11 conflict prompts, all resolved) are presented as achieved, but the beta window is Nov 18-30 and today is 2026-10-26. The safety evidence the gate relies on cannot exist yet.
attacks.evidence: 'Nov 18-30: public opt-in beta branch ... 0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts, all resolved by players.'

attacks.claim: Monitoring has no alert for the failure paths behind the 'never lose a save' guarantee: 'could not be read' rejections, token-mint failures, Steam/EOS validation errors, link failures, and the deletion jobs. Silent failure would go unnoticed.
attacks.evidence: 'Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%, any spike in restores > 3x the beta rate.'

attacks.claim: Replay protection for the Steam session ticket and Epic EOS token (single use, nonce, freshness window) is not described. The token is used only at link time.
attacks.evidence: 'validates the Steam session ticket and Epic EOS token server-side, then stores the link' / ABSENT: replay protection

attacks.claim: The checksum is unkeyed, so it does not prove authenticity. No client-side size or parser limit is stated for downloaded blobs; the 2 MB cap applies only to uploads.
attacks.evidence: 'The client verifies the save's checksum and v3 schema before loading' / ABSENT: client-side size cap on downloads

attacks.claim: Rate limits cover only save uploads. Link, unlink, token minting and restore endpoints have no stated limits.
attacks.evidence: '60 uploads per hour per player' / ABSENT: limits on link, unlink, token and restore

attacks.claim: The one-link-per-store-account rule is stated but not enforced atomically. Concurrent link requests could race and create duplicate links.
attacks.evidence: 'Each store account can be in at most one link.' / ABSENT: unique constraint or transaction

attacks.claim: Access control for changing server config (kill switch, budget-linked flip) is unspecified. Production config is also used by QA and sandbox builds, and whether those builds contain server secrets is not stated.
attacks.evidence: 'Kill switch cross_save_enabled=false (server config...)' / 'pointed at the production Cross-Save backend with the production config'

attacks.claim: There is no account-closure path for linked Steam or Epic accounts, and no access controls, pseudonymisation or retention are stated for dashboard data that maps players across stores.
attacks.evidence: 'Dashboard: link success rate, sync errors by type, conflict prompts, restore usage' / ABSENT: internal access and retention rules

attacks.claim: No access or portability route is described for server-held Steam/Epic IDs, save blobs and sync.meta, which GDPR Articles 15 and 20 require.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any access or export procedure. Only 'Unlink and delete cloud saves' is described.

attacks.claim: The claim that Steam needs no listing change for a feature that shares player data with the studio backend is asserted without a platform policy reference.
attacks.evidence: 'Steam requires no listing change.'

attacks.claim: Cross-Save identity depends entirely on Steam and EOS APIs, with no described degraded path if either identity service changes or is withdrawn. The feature is optional and the game stays playable, which limits the impact.
attacks.evidence: 'Our backend validates the Steam session ticket and Epic EOS token server-side' / ABSENT: fallback or plan if either identity API is discontinued

attacks.claim: No export format, migration path or self-hosting option is described for the backend. EU residency is stated only for save and link storage, not for logs, backups, monitoring or billing.
attacks.evidence: 'Storage region: EU (Frankfurt) for all players.' / ABSENT: export format, self-host definition, residency for logs and backups

attacks.claim: No retry, backoff or 429 handling is specified. Retries could exhaust the 60-uploads-per-hour limit, leaving saves unsynced. Local saves are kept, so this is not data loss.
attacks.evidence: '60 uploads per hour per player' / ABSENT: retry and backoff policy and 429 handling

attacks.claim: The ~$90/month egress figure has no stated assumptions for launch-time downloads. Abuse ceilings are per-player only, with no global or per-IP limit.
attacks.evidence: 'Requests and egress ~$90/month.' / 'On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older.'

attacks.claim: The upload trigger is not defined. Only download-on-launch and 'syncs next launch' are specified, so progress from a long session is not pushed until the next launch.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: upload trigger. 'play continues on the local save and syncs next launch'

attacks.claim: The conflict prompt is forced two-choice with no described defer or dismiss path, and no behaviour for closing it.
attacks.evidence: 'If both changed since last sync, the game asks ... Nothing is overwritten without that choice.'

attacks.claim: The value case rests on a 60% opt-in assumption with no beta opt-in rate or dual-store ownership figure.
attacks.evidence: 'forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in' / ABSENT: opt-in rate or dual-store owner count

attacks.claim: Screen-reader checks cover only the conflict prompt. The restore version list and the Steam/Epic sign-in handoff have no assistive-technology result.
attacks.evidence: 'screen narration for the conflict prompt' / QA row 'Restore from server versions 1-5 and local backups 1-3' has no AT result

attacks.claim: Forward compatibility relies on 1.3 ignoring unknown options keys and the sidecar, which is an assumption about a shipped binary. Bundling sync with modifiers and 31 fixes couples the rollback of unrelated changes.
attacks.evidence: 'Modifiers are stored in the existing v3 options map, whose unknown keys 1.3 already ignores.'

attacks.claim: The 24-month deletion job and the 60 uploads/hour limit have no QA evidence, and their effects on heavy legitimate players are unverified. The cleanup job's scan and batching are also unspecified.
attacks.evidence: 'Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted' / '60 uploads per hour per player' (no test row)
